planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost; this slow-germinating Guyanese landrace rewards patience and steady bottom heat.

directions: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since germination is slower and less even than most peppers; transplant only after nights stay warm. This heirloom from Guyana produces marble-sized, perfectly round fruit that dangle upright like tiny berries, ripening from pale green through orange to bright red on a compact, heavily branched bush. Heat runs fierce and fruity, typically well into habanero territory, and the little pods are the signature ingredient in Guyanese pepper sauce as well as a favorite for pickling whole. In frost-free gardens the plant persists as a short-lived shrubby perennial; elsewhere grow it as a warm-season annual and pick continuously to keep new flowers setting.
sources: Slow Food Foundation — Ark of Taste
